# Proof

> Privacy-first CV editor that compiles beautiful PDFs using Typst. CV data is stored in the browser and compiled to PDF entirely client-side via a WebAssembly build of Typst — nothing is ever sent to a server.

Proof allows users to maintain their CV as structured JSON, choose from 10 professional templates (Default, Modern, Minimal, Sidebar, Compact, Banner, Timeline, Academic, Tech, Editorial), customise layout and style through a visual editor, and download high-quality typeset PDFs.

## Docs

- [CV JSON Schema & Full Reference](/for-llms): Complete specification for CV content JSON, layout structure, and all style parameters — the primary reference for generating importable CV data
- [Editor](/editor): The visual editor (browser-based, no account required)

## Quick start for agents

To help a user create a CV for Proof:

1. Collect their information (name, headline, contact, work history, education, skills, etc.)
2. Produce a JSON file conforming to the CV JSON schema at /for-llms
3. The user imports it via the "↑ Import" button in the editor sidebar
4. They pick a template, customise style, and generate their PDF

## CV JSON — top-level fields

- `identity` — name (string, required), headline (string), contact (array of {type, value, key})
- `summary` — plain text; separate paragraphs with \n\n
- `experience` — array: title, subtitle (Company · Location), period, highlights[], tags[]
- `education` — array: title, subtitle (Degree · Field), period, description
- `skills` — array of groups: {name, entries[]}
- `languages` — array: {title, subtitle}
- `certifications` — array: {title, subtitle, tags[]}
- `awards` — array: {title, subtitle, description}
- `side_projects` — array: {title, subtitle, description, tags[]}
- `core_strengths` — array of short strings, rendered as pills
- `leadership_profile` — single object (not an array): {subtitle, highlights[]}

Contact types: email, phone, location, linkedin, github, medium, facebook, web

Links in text fields use Markdown syntax: [text](https://url) or [text](#section-id) for internal PDF jumps.

## Templates

- `default` — clean split header, sections configurable via layout JSON
- `modern` — accent keyline top border, two-tone name, filled pills
- `minimal` — no rules, typography-only structure
- `sidebar` — dark navy sidebar (contact, skills, languages, certifications) + main column
- `compact` — dense two-column body, fits a long CV on one page
- `banner` — full-width dark header band, filled stack pills
- `timeline` — experience on a dated rail with circular markers
- `academic` — centred formal layout; Experience and Side Projects render in an academic-CV citation style (organisation first, numbered entries) while keeping the standard translated section headings
- `tech` — monospace `//`-prefixed section headers, flat tag grid for skills
- `editorial` — magazine-style large italic display name, narrow meta column
